name: Employment

subjectOf.text: Private fund advisers in the sample did not terminate existing employment relationships, and only few severed advising relationships, changed fund legal structure, liquidated positions, changed investment styles or portfolio structure, or closed funds to new investors.
subjectOf.abstract: Private fund advisers in the sample did not terminate existing employment relationships. Few respondents severed an advising relationship, changed funds' (legal) structure, liquidated positions, changed investment styles, changed portfolio structure, or closed funds to new investors.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915

subjectOf.text: Whether automation actually displaces employment turns on more than technical feasibility: technology costs, labor market dynamics, economic benefits, and regulatory and social acceptance all condition the outcome.
subjectOf.abstract: The impact of automation on employment extends beyond technical feasibility, encompassing factors such as technology costs, labor market dynamics, economic benefits, and regulatory and social acceptance.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Quantum Economy and the Future of Work (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4900880

subjectOf.text: Developing nations can leapfrog to newer technologies without intermediate steps, but the same transition exposes them to increased global competition for work displaced in developed economies, so leapfrogging does not by itself secure employment gains.
subjectOf.abstract: While developing nations can leapfrog, they also face significant challenges, as job displacement in developed economies could lead to increased global competition for certain types of work, potentially affecting employment opportunities in developing nations.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Quantum Economy and the Future of Work (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4900880
